## TL;DR

The desktop board now applies the phone queue's `sort` and shows every URL value
it cannot apply as a notice chip, so nothing is dropped silently at 768 or 1280 px.
The phone queue keeps owning these values at 375 px. Two review rounds and a merge
of main (which brought #1259's board search box) are folded in. The scoped
`repoos check --changed main` passes on the merged tree. The remaining risk is
the server's time budget for the full check, which has timed out twice.

## Work and rationale

The #1257 QA pass found two gaps: `sort=oldest` from the phone queue did nothing
on the board, and `?status=attention|held|archived|human|all` showed every task
with no chip. The task allowed applying each value or noticing it, and I chose per
value.

- **Sort is applied.** A valid `sort=newest|oldest` orders every column by last
  update, through `sortWorkQueueTasks`, which the phone queue also calls now. A
  "Sort: Oldest updated" chip shows it. Without `sort`, the board's own Sort
  control applies.
- **Status is noticed.** The board shows only the six status columns. Phone-only
  values, and anything else the board cannot apply, get an "Ignored filter" chip in
  the dashed style of the existing priority and mine notices. Applying them on the
  board would have meant reimplementing the held, archived and human lists there.
- **Clear covers what the bar shows.** It removes the five queue keys, the URL sort
  and any status the board cannot apply. A single valid board column stays, since it
  has its own bar.
- **The chip bar is desktop-only.** `WorkView` renders it in the non-narrow branch,
  so the phone never shows a notice for a value its own queue applies.

### Review round 2

1. **The Sort control disagreed with the board.** The dropdown followed the store
   while the columns followed the URL. It now clears its model value while a URL
   sort is set, and shows the sort's label as the placeholder. A jsdom case stubs
   `Select` and checks the bound value is `null`, with the board oldest-first.
2. **Repeated or bare status was silently dropped.** `firstString` took the first
   entry of `?status=ready&status=held`, a board column, so nothing was noticed. The
   check now reads the raw value. Repeated, bare and empty status get notices ("use
   one status" for repeats), and Clear removes them.
3. **An ignored sort stuck until Clear.** Picking a sort in the control now drops
   any `sort` key in the URL, applied or ignored.
4. **Pipeline note.** It now reads "This view doesn't apply these filters or sort".

### Merge of main

Main had moved, and #1259 added a board search box that writes `q` through
`withWorkQueueSearch`. Conflicts were in `WorkView.vue`,
`work-queue-filters.test.ts`, the QA doc and the task file. Each side was additive,
so I kept both: my sort and status code alongside main's search. The task file
took main's copy. Other tasks' `work/*.md` in the worktree had stale edits, which
I set to main's copy, since a task branch carries only its own files. The merge
commit is `68400159c`.

## Approaches tried

I first considered applying every status value on the board, and rejected it
because the board already has its own hidden-category toggles, so the notice was
the smaller correct fix. For Clear I first kept `sort` out, matching the earlier
QA. That left an applied sort with no way to remove it from the bar, so Clear now
removes it and the QA doc says so.

For the dropdown I considered adding an "oldest" option to the shared `SortOrder`
list. That list also feeds the story panel, so I used a placeholder instead.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Full-suite timeouts.** The scoped tests step failed three times, each run with
  a different set of 30-second timeouts (`agent-review`, `debugger-integration`,
  `task-watchdog`, several WebKit cases in `stories-inbox-search-qa-browser`,
  `offline-slow-network-browser`, `releases-publish-failures-browser`). Every
  failing file passed when run alone (110 of 110, then 44 of 44). None touches the
  work board. I read this as parallel-load timing, not a regression, but I did not
  prove it on an idle machine. The post-merge scoped `repoos check` passed in full.
- **Server finalization timed out** ("deadline exceeded") on the first retry, and the
  server's check was still in its verify step when I last looked. The draft was then
  reported missing at the review step, so I rewrote it.
- The 768 and 1280 px cases are WebKit viewport emulations. Touch targets and the
  native shell still need a real device.

## Key learnings

- A URL value is handled only if every view that reads it applies it or says so.
  The board's notice path must not run on the phone, where the value is applied.
- Read the raw route value, not a first-element helper, or repeated keys vanish.
- Clear must remove what its bar displays, or a chip cannot be removed from the bar.
- RepoOS consumes the report draft during a handoff attempt, so a draft needs
  rewriting for each request.
